1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

Learned A.G.A. informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter, including upto date case diary, and the investigation in this case, so far as the applicant is concerned, is pending.
2.

This application has been moved by the applicant-Kapil Dev for grant of anticipatory bail in FIR/Case Crime No.0886 of 2023, under sections 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC read with section 6/9 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, lodged at police station Kotwali, district Unnao.

It is vehemently submitted that the whole evidence, which is available against the applicant, is the confessional statement of co-accused- Kunal Kumar Paswan and beyond that there is no iota of evidence, which may connect the applicant with the crime.

It is vehemently submitted that co-accused- Kunal Kumar Paswan has been granted regular bail by this court vide order passed in criminal misc. bail application no.1418 of 2024 and even if the case of the prosecution is believed as it is, there is no requirement of custodial interrogation of the applicant and, it appears that on account of misinterpretation of section 170 CrPC, the investigating officer though has completed investigation but is not filing the charge-sheet without arrest of the applicant while the arrest of the application is not required for the purpose of filing of charge-sheet as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation and others : (2021) 10 SCC 773 and Siddharth v. State of UP : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 615.
4.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the applicant is not having any previous criminal record to his credit and is he ready to cooperate in the investigation and would remain present before the investigating officer as and when his presence would be required and there is no apprehension that after being released on anticipatory bail, he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

5. Considering the fact that co-accused- Kunal Kumar Paswan is shown to have been arrested from the examination centre, allegedly impersonating the applicant and only evidence against the applicant which has been placed before this court is the confessional statement of co-accused- Kunal Kumar Paswal, who has been enlarged on regular bail by this court, the applicant is not having previous criminal antecedents, having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra (2011) 1 SCC 694 as well as in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
(2020) 5 SCC 1, Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Ors. v. State of Punjab MANU/SC/0215/1980 : 1980 (2)
SCC 565 and in Nathu Singh Vs State of U.P. and Others, 2021(6) SCC 64, MANU/SC/0360/2021, a case for anticipatory bail is made out in favour of the applicant.
6.

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant shall not leave the District concerned without the previous permission of the Court.
(iv). The applicant if not arrested earlier, shall surrender before the trial court within 20 days from today i.e. on or before 03.04.2024 and will cooperate in the trial.

(v). The applicant shall cooperate in the investigation and will make himself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact, if the case is directed to be further investigated.
(vi). The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his release on anticipatory bail.

(vii). The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and especially when the prosecution witnesses are present in court.
(viii).

The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
7.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of any of the condition placed above is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and shall proceed against him in accordance with law.

8. It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the proceedings before the trial court in any manner.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, the instant anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of the applicant- Kapil Dev is allowed and it is provided that in the event of arrest of the applicant, involved in the above noted case, under any process of the trial court or on his surrender/appearance before the trial court within 20 days from today i.e. on or before 02.04.2024, whichever is earlier, he shall be released forthwith on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court concerned, subject to the following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation or for discovery of any fact by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
